summary: Jun Fujii is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo. He served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University from around 2010 to 2013.

Jun Takashima specializes in Indology, religious studies, and computational fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, and later held positions at Aichi Prefectural University, Toyo University, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as professor in 2020.

Jun Yang works in linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Yang's affiliations include serving as a Senior Lecturer in Chinese Language at the University of Chicago and as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University, both attested in 2026.

Jundo Nagashima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seitatsu Matsunami, Alexis Sanderson, and doctoral supervisor Paul Williams at the University of Bristol. Nagashima served as a lecturer at Taisho University, attested between 2006 and 2017.

June McDaniel specializes in Indology and religious studies, earning an MTS from Emory University and a Ph.D. from the University of Chicago. She has held posts at the College of Charleston, attested in 2000 and 2015 as a professor.

Junglan Bang specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. After studying under Seung-suk Jung and Sungdoo Ahn at Dongguk University, Bang completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson and held a visiting researcher post at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Ha completed a master's degree at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and earned a PhD at Duke University under the supervision of Stanley Abe, attested in 2016.

Junjirō Takakusu was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Ryukoku, Oxford, Berlin, and Leipzig under Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He was a professor and president at the University of Tokyo.

Junkei Washio was a Buddhist studies and history and archaeology scholar who studied at Toyo University from around 1887 to 1890. He held professorships at Toyo University and Komazawa University, and also taught at Sendan-Rin School.

Junkichi Imanishi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Hokkaido University, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Junko Matsumura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Matsumura completed an MA in Asian Studies at the Australian National University and a doctoral dissertation at the University of Göttingen, later serving as professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Junko Minamoto is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed a master's degree at Ryukoku University, pursued doctoral studies at Otani University, and served as a commissioned researcher at Kansai University.
Junko Sakamoto-Gotō works in Indology and linguistics. Her academic career includes posts at Tohoku University, attested in 2005, and Ryukoku University, attested in 2015.

Junmai Zhang was a philosopher and Sinologist who studied under Qichao Liang, at Waseda University, and at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held academic posts at Peking University from around 1916 to 1918 and at Tsinghua University.

Junsho Kato is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo, KU Leuven, and under Étienne Lamotte. He held posts as professor at Nishogakusha University and professor of Indian culture at Nagoya University.

Juntarō Ishihama was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kansai University and held academic posts at Ryukoku University (circa 1923–1945) and Kansai University (circa 1948–1968).
Junzo Inagaki is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. Inagaki studied under Shoshin Fukihara and served as a section chief (課長) at Otani University.
Juri Lotman was a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. He completed his studies at Saint Petersburg State University and held a post at the University of Tartu beginning in 1954.
Juro Watanabe is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and held a post at the University of Tsukuba, attested between 1989 and 1990.

Justin McDaniel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He served as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and holds an endowed professorship in the humanities at the University of Pennsylvania.
